events.title: Laravel 3.2 released
events.summary: Laravel migrated core request/response handling to Symfony's HttpFoundation component.
events.about: Instead of maintaining its own HTTP layer, Laravel adopted Symfony's battle-tested request/response objects. For developers: handling cookies, headers, and responses works the same way across Symfony, Laravel, and other PHP tools — less duplicated code in the PHP ecosystem.

narrative.whyChosen: This is the clearest example of Laravel embracing Symfony instead of maintaining parallel HTTP stacks.
narrative.whyImportant: Shared components meant PHP developers could move between Laravel, Symfony, and Drupal with familiar HTTP primitives.
narrative.problemSolved: Maintaining custom request/response code duplicated effort across the PHP ecosystem.
